story: Alex stared at the blank screen, his fingers hovering tremulously above the keyboard like broken wings. The clock ticked loudly, each second a hammer blow against his fraying sanity as the deadline loomed closer. He scrubbed at his eyes, leaving red marks on his pale skin, trying to wipe away the fog that clouded his thoughts. A dry heave rose in his throat, choking off any coherent sentence he might have formed. He pushed the chair back abruptly, the screech echoing in the silent room, and paced the narrow floor until his legs gave out beneath him.

Alex stared at the blank screen, fingers trembling against the cold keyboard as the clock ticked past midnight. The rent notice lay crumpled in his pocket, a heavy reminder of the eviction looming just days away. He scrolled through endless job listings, each rejection email stinging like a fresh wound on his already frayed nerves. Sweat prickled along his hairline, soaking into his collar while his heart hammered against his ribs like a trapped bird. He clenched his jaw, forcing himself to keep typing despite the burning exhaustion that threatened to swallow him whole. Every keystroke felt like a gamble, a fragile thread holding back the inevitable collapse of his carefully constructed life.

Alex stared at the blinking cursor, his fingers hovering inches above the keyboard like frightened birds. The deadline had passed an hour ago, and the silence in the room felt heavy, pressing against his eardrums with suffocating weight. He tried to recall the solution, but his mind was a blank, white wall that refused to yield any answers. Sweat prickled along his hairline, cooling uncomfortably on his neck as he realized the data he needed had been corrupted. With a trembling hand, he reached for the phone, dialing a number he had sworn never to call, his breath coming in shallow, ragged gasps that offered no relief to the crushing pressure in his chest.
